cohort: The study included 594 mother-neonate pairs with live neonates delivered during the study period, excluding stillborns, neonates with major congenital malformations, and neonates whose mothers died during birth.
finding: The prevalence of birth trauma was 13.13%, with prolonged labour, birth weight >4 kg, vacuum delivery, forceps delivery, and shoulder dystocia identified as significant risk factors.
mod_finding: Vacuum delivery and forceps delivery were identified as significant risk factors for birth trauma.
birth_weight: Live neonates of all weights were included, and birth weight >4 kg was identified as a risk factor.
